method: Independent confirm assessment. Each component was read on the current recursive input route (the entry, its declared annex proof and every cross-referenced result) and compared item by item with the held source at the printed pages listed in source_locators (printed page + 8 = PDF page in both held PDFs). Author scope records, other assessments, return files and ledger prose were not consulted; component metadata (entry labels, line spans, declared treatments) was read from the completion work queue, whose unit record also displayed the title line of an author scope note, and nothing beyond that line was read. Unmapped source material was not treated as owed except in the one X- duty recorded. Coverage only; no correctness acceptance is implied.

components.gap: The source's name for the outcome set is not supplied: Grinstead-Snell Definition 1.1 (printed p. 18) calls the set of possible outcomes the sample space (and calls a random variable on a finite or countably infinite sample space discrete). The entry introduces Omega only as a finite set of outcomes; the term 'sample space', which later P15 chapters and proofs on the route use without definition, is never defined or indexed.

components.gap: Tree diagrams and tree measures are not presented. Grinstead-Snell model a multistage experiment by a tree whose paths are outcomes (Tree Diagrams, Example 1.10, Fig. 1.8, printed pp. 24-25), read branch weights as conditional probabilities and obtain inverse (Bayes) probabilities from the reversed tree (Example 4.5, Figs. 4.1-4.2, printed pp. 135-136), and recommend a tree-measure calculation over Bayes' formula when the hypotheses are few (printed p. 146). The handbook gives only the algebraic multiplication and chain rules (thm:p15-finite-conditioning-laws) and, elsewhere, the abstract kernel construction (thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure); no route file presents the tree-measure method or the reverse-tree computation.

components.gap: The source's odds definition is narrowed. Grinstead-Snell Definition 1.4 (printed p. 28) states odds in favour as r:s with r/s = p/(1-p), notes that only the ratio matters (r to s means r/s to 1), and gives the inverse p = r/(r+s); it motivates odds by willingness to bet (accepting a 2-to-1 bet on an event means probability 2/3) and calls a bet at the stated odds fair (Example 1.12). The entry defines only the ratio P(G)/(1-P(G)); the r:s form, the inverse conversion and the betting interpretation are absent from the route.

components.gap: The source's equivalent form of mutual independence is not supplied. Grinstead-Snell Definition 4.2 (printed p. 141) states that A_1, ..., A_n are mutually independent exactly when the full intersection factorizes for every choice of B_j equal to A_j or to its complement. The route proves only the forward direction (complements of independent events stay independent: thm:p15-independence-basic item 2; the two-event case in thm:p15-finite-independence-laws); that factorization over all complement patterns of the whole family implies independence of every subfamily is neither stated nor proved.

components.gap: The source's existence convention for expectation is not preserved. Grinstead-Snell Definition 6.1 (printed p. 226) defines E(X) for a discrete X on a finite or countably infinite sample space only when the sum of x m(x) converges absolutely, and otherwise says that X has no expected value (Example 6.3, St. Petersburg payoff, printed p. 227). The entry is restricted to finite spaces, and the route's countable treatment (def:p15-expectation-integral, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral) uses the extended convention (a nonnegative variable may have expectation +infinity) without recording or reconciling the source's absolute-convergence variant.

components.gap: Durrett's notation for special cases (pp. 23-24) is not set out: the integral of f(x) dx for Lebesgue measure on R^d, the integral from a to b of f(x) dx for E = [a, b], the integral of f(x) dG(x) for the Stieltjes measure of G, and a sum of f(i) over i for counting measure. The integration chapter states none of these conventions; the route later writes dx and integrals from a to b without stating them (the dG and counting-measure readings appear only in def:p15-convolution-law and the product-measures annex).

Durrett (p. 26) notes that on a space of finite measure convergence in measure is a weaker assumption than a.e. convergence. The entry defines both modes without comparing them, and the route proves the implication only for probability spaces (thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-as-probability item 1), not for finite measures.
